Writing Skills

Writing clear nursing notes, reports and records — SOAP, accuracy and legal rules.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Write a clear nursing note
  • Use the SOAP method
  • State legal rules for documentation

In simple words

Writing in nursing means recording what you did, observed and planned. Records are legal documents — if it is not written, it is not done.

Good records are clear, accurate, dated, timed and signed. They protect the patient and the nurse.

SOAP method

Part What to write Example
S – Subjective What the patient says “I have pain in my chest”
O – Objective What you measure or see “BP 150/90, pulse 96”
A – Assessment Your conclusion “Possible cardiac pain”
P – Plan What you will do “Inform doctor, give oxygen as ordered”

Legal rules for documentation

  • Write in ink; never use pencil.
  • Do not erase — draw one line through errors, initial and date.
  • Write facts, not opinions (“patient cried” not “patient is difficult”).
  • Sign every entry with your name and designation.
  • Record the time of every entry.
  • Never write for someone else or pre-write ahead of time.

🔴 Documentation rule

If it is not written, it is not done. Records are legal documents — write facts, date, time and sign every entry.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Nursing notes — write after every important observation or procedure.
  • Incident reports — record what happened, who was involved and what you did.
  • Handover notes — give the next shift accurate, written information.
  • Discharge summaries — write what the patient and family need to do at home.
  • Legal cases — your record may be used in court; make it truthful and complete.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Nursing records are legal documents — if not written, it is not done.
  2. SOAP: Subjective (patient says), Objective (you see), Assessment (conclusion), Plan (action).
  3. Write in ink; date, time and sign every entry.
  4. Do not erase — cross out errors with one line, initial and date.
  5. Write facts, not opinions.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Never pre-write entries ahead of time.
  2. Never write for someone else.
  3. Accurate records protect both patient and nurse.

📌 Memory trick

SOAP = “Says, Observes, Assesses, Plans.”

60-second revision

  • Records are legal; if not written, not done.
  • SOAP: Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan.
  • Ink, date, time, sign every entry.
  • Cross out errors with one line, initial and date.
  • Facts not opinions.

Test yourself

In SOAP, 'O' stands for:

Answer: B. O is Objective — what you observe or measure.

If you make a writing error, you should:

Answer: B. Cross out errors with a single line, then initial and date — never erase.

Documentation should include:

Answer: B. Write facts with date, time and signature; avoid opinions.

Which is part of the Plan in SOAP?

Answer: B. Plan is what you will do next for the patient.

Records should be signed by:

Answer: B. Each entry is signed by the nurse who made it, with designation.
